_about: THE SUN: the one light that every shadow, shaded roof and slope, and the shadow-side pen follows. ONE SOURCE (2026-10-11): scripts/world/sun.gd (Sun.current()) reads this file, and RenderParams (P.sunAz, P.elev), UiStyle and FxStyle (shadow_dir, sun_len, the sun_direction and sun_elevation params) and InkCanvas's pen all ask it; nothing else holds a copy. MODE 'clock_at_start' IS THE GAME'S SUN (decision sun-time, 2026-10-11, Alex: "Fixed time at start" and "Every shadow follows"): the sun comes from a time of day, is picked ONCE when the mission starts and does not move during it, and EVERY shadow follows that one sun. The hour is the HOST'S clock at the mission start (a Local game's own), sent to a client with the start so that both peers bake one map (PROPOSED, scripts/net/mission_start.gd); a scenario may pin an hour ('sun_hour' in its JSON; PROPOSED); the tests never read the machine's clock (scripts/test_support/test_case.gd pins the sun). MODE 'fixed' STAYS AS A SWITCH: today's sun, unchanged, from the north-west (315), elevation 46, as the design doc's Style guide > Light and shadow says (the prototype's own values). The model itself (the numbers of the 'clock' block) is the builder BS's PROPOSAL from Alex's playtest note ('Lets have the tree shadows change. The easiest thing to do would be to use the current time of day and use that to select the shadow angles. Show me some options before commiting this.'), bent by Alex's answers on the board: the night hours FOLD, "the sun should be coming from north side to keep shadows below the objects not above", "reduce the distance a bit". AZIMUTH IS A COMPASS BEARING with the map's north up: 0 north, 90 east, 180 south, 270 west; 315 is the north-west, so a shadow falls to the south-east (the prototype's shadowDir is (azimuth + 90) degrees on the screen). The knobs sun_mode, sun_hour and sun_scope in scripts/debug/debug_settings.gd (INKWOOD_SUN_MODE=fixed INKWOOD_SUN_HOUR=9) override the three switches below at run time; 'data' there means this file. Keys that begin with an underscore are notes; a value record with a 'decision' is Alex's choice, one with '_proposed' is not yet.

mode._reason: clock_at_start = the time-of-day model (the 'clock' block), the sun taken ONCE when the mission starts and held for the whole mission, so the map bakes once (Alex, decision sun-time: "Fixed time at start"). It became the default on 2026-10-11 when the sun went live. fixed = today's sun (the 'fixed' block below), kept as a switch: INKWOOD_SUN_MODE=fixed, or a scenario or a test asking for it.

scope._reason: clock_at_start only. all = every shadow follows the one sun (ALEX, decision sun-time: "Every shadow follows"). trees = ONLY the trees' cast shadows take the clock's sun and everything else (terrain scarps, structures, units, the shadow-side pen) keeps the fixed sun: it exists only to draw the board's 'why not' frame, that two suns on one map break the look. Not meant for play.

hour._reason: the local hour, 0 to 24 (9.5 is half past nine), the clock model is asked for when hour_source is 'data': a test's, a board's, or a game started where the clock is not asked. Noon, the middle of the day. Not what the game uses: the game's hour_source is 'system'.

hour_source._reason: PROPOSED. system = the time of day on the machine that STARTS the mission, read once (Alex's suggestion: "use the current time of day"); in co-op that machine is the HOST, and its hour is sent to the client with the start (scripts/net/mission_start.gd, Sun.begin_mission / Sun.apply_start), so both see one map and a client never reads its own clock. data = the 'hour' above. A scenario's 'sun_hour' and the sun_hour knob outrank this.

fixed._about: Today's sun, copied from the prototype's parameters (design doc, Prototype > Parameters and defaults; Style guide > Light and shadow). Not a proposal.

clock._about: THE TIME-OF-DAY MODEL. The sun rises in the north-east, is due north at the middle of the day and sets in the north-west, the map's north up (a sun that never gets south of the objects, so every shadow falls BELOW its object on the map, with a southward part at every hour: Alex, "the sun should be coming from north side to keep shadows below the objects not above"). The bearing runs from rise_azimuth_deg at sunrise_hour to set_azimuth_deg at sunset_hour in a straight line over the hours (45 -> 0 -> -45, the last written as a negative bearing so that the line passes through north, and read as 315). The height follows a sine arc, noon_elevation_deg at the middle of the day and 0 at sunrise and sunset. THE SHADOW'S LENGTH, 1 / tan(elevation) times the height of the thing, is clamped to max_shadow_len so that dawn and dusk shadows stay readable; the elevation the readers see is the one that length belongs to, so every reader that works out 1 / tan(elevation) gets the clamped length. Today's fixed sun is 46 degrees (length 0.97). At 60 degrees noon the length is 0.58. THE HOURS (computed, not chosen): with the fold rule the 24 hours lie on the arc (midnight is sunrise's sun, 06:00 the bearing 22 sun at 42 degrees, noon is noon), so the shadows are at the clamp, 2.0 times the height, for seven hours of the real day (20:30 to 03:30), between 1.0 and 2.0 for 03:30 to 06:08 and 17:52 to 20:30, and shorter than today's 0.97 from 06:08 to 17:52, down to 0.58 at noon.

sunrise_hour._reason: equinox-simple: a 12-hour day. A season or a latitude is not modelled.

rise_azimuth_deg._reason: PROPOSED numbers on Alex's direction (north side). 45 = north-east: the same slant as today's fixed sun (315, north-west) mirrored, so no hour of the day throws a shadow more sideways than the game already shows; every shadow keeps cos(45) = 0.71 of its length going down the map. A wider swing would send them more sideways, a narrower one would make the day's light too alike.

set_azimuth_deg._reason: -45 is 315, the north-west: today's fixed sun, reached at sunset. Written negative so that the straight line from rise to set goes through north (0) at noon and not through south.

noon_elevation_deg._reason: a mid-latitude spring or autumn noon. Higher than today's 46 so that the middle of the day has the shortest shadows, and not so high that they vanish under the trees. Kept as it was on the board: with the shorter clamp below the arc already reads shorter, so there was no reason to move it.

max_shadow_len._reason: PROPOSED number on Alex's "reduce the distance a bit": the longest shadow per unit of height is 2.0, a 26.6 degree sun, instead of the board's 3.0 (18.4 degrees). A tree's shadow is at most twice its height and a plane's gap to its shadow at most twice the 1% rule's; the lit side stays most of the picture.

night._reason: ALEX chose fold on the board (the board's proposal, quoted: "with clamp, a game played at any hour from 18:00 to 06:00, half of all hours, gets the dawn-or-dusk sun with the longest shadows the model has; fold spreads them"). fold = the 24 hours laid on the day arc (midnight is sunrise's sun, 6:00 the bearing 22 sun at 42 degrees, 12:00 noon, 18:00 the bearing 338 sun, 24:00 sunset's), so the sun always moves and no hour is left out. clamp = the nearest daytime hour (before 6:00 the 6:00 sun, after 18:00 the 18:00 sun): kept as the other setting, and for the board.
